title: 1956 AHSME Problem 35
statement: A rhombus is formed by two radii and two chords of a circle whose radius is \(16\) feet. The area of the rhombus in square feet is:

solutions.text:
All four sides of the rhombus equal the circle’s radius, \(16.\) A chord of length equal to the radius forms an equilateral triangle with the two radii to its endpoints, so the included central angle is \(60^\circ.\) Therefore the rhombus has area \[ \begin{aligned} 16^2\sin60^\circ &=256\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\ &=128\sqrt3. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Every side of the rhombus has length \(16,\) so each chord equals the radius
A chord equal to the radius subtends a \(60^\circ\) central angle; use \(s^2\sin\theta\)
